dance: Wilt thou go to the barracks, Johnny?

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

observation.setting: outdoor lawn at a Highland games event with a wooden dance platform, grandstands, and flags in the background
observation.dancers: two female dancers and one male bagpiper standing to the side
observation.formation_and_space: side-by-side duo facing forward on a square wooden platform, staying in place without traveling across the grass
observation.posture: upright, erect torso, weight shifted dynamically onto ball of feet with elevated heels
observation.footwork: fast springing steps, pointing and extending one foot while hopping or springing on the supporting leg in sync with the beat
observation.arms_and_hands: one arm curved upward overhead with fingers slightly rounded, the other hand on the hip, alternating or matching between dancers
observation.hips_and_torso: torso remains upright and stable while legs move independently; hips rotate slightly with leg extensions
observation.levels_jumps_turns: frequent vertical springing jumps on spot, high extensions of working legs, no floor work
observation.costume_and_props: blue jackets, tartan kilts and hose, ghillie brogues, competition numbers pinned on kilts; bagpipe played by musician
observation.cannot_infer: exact foot pressure, subtle ankle articulation obscured by footwear and resolution

signature_moments.what: simultaneous springing hop with one leg extended outward and the opposite arm raised overhead
rapid continuous springing on toes while extending the working leg forward and back in mid-air
extended leg pointing to the side while maintaining high half-toe balance and overhead arm position
light vertical elevation with knees apart in mid-air before landing precisely on half-toe
